where: scripts/qa-journey-shell.mjs: watch() (its pageerror handler) and the final assertion "11.1 no script error and no hydration warning on any page the drive opened"
problem: watch() counts every pageerror except "ResizeObserver loop". That includes React 19's development-only error "Failed to execute 'measure' on 'Performance': '<zero-width space>AccountHubPage' cannot have a negative time stamp.", which the repo has already measured hitting /account on a local dev server. This drive only ever runs against a dev server and opens /account about 16 times (unread 3, tabs 1, hub 9, overlays 1, plus the warm pass). So 11.1 should be expected to FAIL, and the run would exit 1 over an error a production build cannot throw and no player can meet. That trains the reader to ignore 11.1.
evidence: origin/main (7d4b0ad5, commit 5a87e764, which is newer than the checkout's HEAD 85866b36): scripts/qa-classic-shell-parity.mjs:100-108 says it "hit 6 /account cells on one run of 2d0f56e7 and 16 on one of 55cb61e3, trees that do not touch /account ... A production build has no such measure". The filter is DEV_MEASURE at :109, and isDevMeasure/fileError at :110-112 are wired to page.on("pageerror") at :979 and :1133. The draft's watch() has no such filter.
fix: Copy the parity harness's filter. It already contains no backslash: new RegExp("^Failed to execute 'measure' on 'Performance': '" + String.fromCharCode(0x200b) + "?[A-Za-z0-9_$]+' cannot have a negative time stamp[.]$"). A startsWith/endsWith pair on the same sentence would also work. Put matching page errors in a devOnly list that is printed beside 11.1 and never counted as a FAIL. Keep failing on every other page error and every hydration warning.

where: scripts/qa-journey-shell.mjs: FOCUS_PROBE (halo) and focusTile (ring = !!f && f.visible && (f.outlineOn || f.halo))
problem: For two of the five focus cells, the ring half of the assertion cannot fail. The captioned capsule and the gilt "+ Weka pesa" pill both carry a box-shadow at rest, so halo is true whether or not any focus ring is drawn. If someone removed the outline from either control, the line would still PASS, because only f.visible (the :focus-visible match) is actually tested.
evidence: src/app/globals.css:5925 gives .kp-jbal a resting `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px ...`. src/app/motion.css:446-455 gives .gilt-metal a resting box-shadow. The ring these controls actually draw is an outline: the catch-all :where(a, button, ...):focus-visible at globals.css:2325-2331, .btn:focus-visible at globals.css:1152, and .gilt-metal:focus-visible at motion.css:475-479.
fix: Require outlineOn, since every control in these steps draws an outline ring. Alternatively, read the element's box-shadow before focus and treat halo as true only if the shadow changed.

where: scripts/qa-journey-shell.mjs: checkShell (the classic branch's "no horizontal overflow" line, and every journey call without a scope: the header, tabs, focus and overlays sections)
problem: On classic tiles the overflow line can never FAIL. It reads only documentElement.scrollWidth - clientWidth, and that is always 0 because html and body both clip, so the line passes without measuring anything. The classic branch never runs CLIP_PROBE. On journey tiles without a scope, CLIP_PROBE sweeps only the journey header and the rail. A page's own control past the edge is therefore never asserted on any tabs-section page (/wallet, /results, /live, /leaderboard, /markets/<id>, /updown/<id>, and the rest), or on the header, focus and overlays tiles.
evidence: src/app/globals.css:932-933 (html) and :960-961 (body) both set `overflow-x: clip`. scripts/live/clip.mjs:16-19 records that `documentElement.scrollWidth - clientWidth WAS 0 THROUGHOUT` over controls that were severed. In the draft, checkShell's classic branch is ok(`no horizontal overflow`, s.docOverflow <= 0) with no CLIP_PROBE call, and scope is passed only in the unread, hub, sheet, wallet and tickets sections.
fix: On classic tiles, run CLIP_PROBE over the classic header and rail. CLIP_PROBE falls back to the whole body when its selector is absent, so calling it with "body" also works. On every journey tile, add the #main-content sweep (scope "#main-content") that only the tickets section uses now. Then either drop the docOverflow half or label it as a backstop that cannot fail on its own.

where: scripts/qa-journey-shell.mjs: the whole run (section(), withPage(), openPage(), warm(), post()) and the header's 'CELLS ... about 15 minutes' claim
problem: Nothing bounds the run time. There is no overall deadline and no circuit breaker; only per-call timeouts limit it. The 15-minute estimate assumes a warm server, but the drive's own usage requires a fresh (cold) one.
evidence: Nothing in the file tracks elapsed time across sections or counts consecutive failures. The per-call ceilings are: goto 240 s plus hydrate 120 s for each of about 81 page loads, post() 300 s, warm() 240 s for each of 19 paths, and noHub() 240 s. Every page.evaluate (settle()'s requestAnimationFrame promise and every probe) has no timeout at all. If the server stops answering mid-run, each remaining load can cost about 360 s, roughly 8 hours in total, while the job holds the heavy-node lock. A healthy run is also tight. Fixed sleeps alone come to about 5 minutes: 262 tiles x (450 ms resize settle + 250 ms shoot settle), 81 loads x 400 ms, 15 sheet/wallet opens x about 1 s, and the 48 s overlay dwell. Add about 81 loads at 4-8 s and 262 probe-and-screenshot passes, and my estimate is about 14-21 minutes on a warm server. The usage requires `rm -rf .next` and a fresh server, so the first compiles of about 20 routes come on top of that. Heavy jobs here run under heavy-node-lock.sh and are never wrapped in an external timeout, so the limit has to be inside the drive.
fix: 1. Add KP_BUDGET_MIN (default 15-20). Check it in section() and before every openPage(); once it is spent, print one BLOCKED line per remaining section or cell, by name. 2. Add a circuit breaker: after 3 consecutive openPage() or post() failures, BLOCK everything left with the reason 'server stopped answering'. 3. Arm one watchdog setTimeout at budget + 5 min that prints the counts and a BLOCKED line, then exits 3; this covers a hung page.evaluate. 4. Move warm() into §0 so cold compiles are paid and timed up front, and restate the time estimate for a cold server.

where: scripts/qa-journey-shell.mjs: the single premise() call at the top, versus ensureMain(), post(), seededSession() and every demoSession() call
problem: The check that the server is local and in-memory runs once at start-up. The real-money seeding runs minutes later with no re-check, leaving a time-of-check to time-of-use gap.
evidence: `const { refuse, health } = await premise(BASE)` is the only premise call. ensureMain() calls /api/dev-test/seed-player-portfolio for the first time at §4, after §0, the classic section (6 loads), the header section (18 loads, 90 tiles) and the sheet section: about 6-9 minutes later. That route runs buyPosition, cashOutPosition, settleMarket({force:true}) and emergencyVoidMarket against the first 12 LIVE non-demo markets (seed-player-portfolio/route.ts:90-190). It is gated only by NODE_ENV, so any `next dev` answers it, including one with a DATABASE_URL. Parallel sessions here start and stop dev servers on the same ports. If :3041 changes hands in that window, the drive would force-settle and void markets in whatever store that server has. /api/health reports uptimeSec (health/route.ts:42), so a restarted or swapped server can be detected.
fix: Put every server-mutating request behind one guard. That covers seed-real-markets, updown-seed, seed-player-portfolio, each demoSession, each seededSession and mintStaffPass. The guard re-runs premise(BASE) and also requires health.uptimeSec >= (start-up uptimeSec + elapsed seconds - a small margin). If either check fails, print REFUSED and exit 2 before sending the request.

where: scripts/qa-journey-shell.mjs: FOCUS_PROBE (halo) and focusTile() (the ring condition)
problem: For the captioned balance and the gold '+ Weka pesa' pill, the assertion that a :focus-visible ring is shown cannot fail. Both controls wear a box-shadow at rest, and the probe counts any box-shadow as a ring.
evidence: FOCUS_PROBE sets `halo: !!cs.boxShadow && cs.boxShadow !== 'none'`. focusTile() passes when `f.visible && (f.outlineOn || f.halo)`. f.visible is always true after a real Tab. `.kp-jbal` has `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px ...` at rest (globals.css:5925), and `.gilt-metal` has `box-shadow: var(--gilt-metal-edge), 0 1px 2px ...` at rest (motion.css:451). So 6 of the 13 focus lines (capsule and pill x sw/en/zh) would still PASS if every focus-visible rule were deleted. This is the 'defensive OR that measures nothing' pattern recorded in live/clip.mjs (E-191).
fix: Read the target's computed outline and box-shadow at rest (before the Tab, or after blur()), then read them again after the Tab. Require an outline (outlineStyle not 'none' and width at least 1px), or else a box-shadow that differs from the resting value. Never accept a bare box-shadow. The product's own rules all draw a 2px outline: the `:where(a, button, ...)` catch-all (globals.css:2325), `.btn:focus-visible` (:1152) and `.gilt-metal:focus-visible` (motion.css:475, kept on purpose by E-129). So requiring the outline is correct and can actually fail.

where: scripts/qa-journey-shell.mjs: openPage() and shoot(), which never hide the Next.js dev overlay
problem: Tiles are shot on `next dev` without hiding the Next.js dev-tools indicator (`nextjs-portal`). At phone widths it covers the rail's first tab, Maswali, which is the tab every tile on / must show as lit.
evidence: next.config.ts sets no devIndicators, and the draft adds no style. The repo's other tile drives that shoot on next dev all hide it: scripts/qa/landing-v3/capture.mjs:112, scripts/live/mobile-visual-drive.mjs:137, scripts/qa/tax-report-drive.mjs:146 and :402, and scripts/qa-house-bots-visual.mjs:302, each with `nextjs-portal{display:none!important}`. The journey rail is fixed at the bottom (journey-tabs.tsx:57), and its first slot is Maswali. That affects about 51 header phone tiles, 6 classic tiles, and the sheet, wallet, focus and overlay tiles on /. The indicator sits in a shadow root, so CLIP_PROBE and RAIL_PROBE cannot see it; only the human reading of the tiles is affected.
fix: In openPage(), after hydration, add `await page.addStyleTag({ content: 'nextjs-portal,[data-nextjs-toast],[data-nextjs-dialog-overlay]{display:none!important}' })`. This is the repo's own line and needs no backslash. Also follow pre-deploy-live-check.mjs:45-50 and FAIL a cell when a real Next error dialog is present, instead of only hiding it.

where: scripts/qa-journey-shell.mjs: `const OUT = process.argv[2] || join(tmpdir(), ...)`, followed by mkdirSync(OUT) and page.screenshot({ path: join(OUT, file) })
problem: Nothing stops the drive writing inside the repository. Whatever outDir it is given is used as-is, including relative paths.
evidence: OUT is taken verbatim from argv[2]. `npm run` runs scripts with cwd set to the package root, so the documented `npm run qa:journey-shell -- <outDir>` with a name like `tiles` puts about 262 untracked PNGs into the worktree. The repo's .gitignore records why that is dangerous: the scripts/live/.shots/ entry notes that 'one [session] has already swept another's untracked files into its own commit', and a push to main deploys live. The lens requires the drive to write nothing in the repo, but today only the default path guarantees that.
fix: Resolve OUT with path.resolve. Compute the repo root as resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..') and rel = relative(root, OUT). If rel is '', or rel does not start with '..' and is not absolute, print `REFUSED: outDir is inside the repository` and exit 2 before premise() or mkdirSync() runs. None of this needs a backslash in the source.

where: scripts/qa-journey-shell.mjs: noHub()
problem: The line '/account renders no hub for a viewer without a pass' passes on any response that lacks the test id: a 500, an error boundary or a redirect to sign-in.
evidence: The check is `ok(..., !html.includes('journey-account-hub'), 'HTTP ' + res.status())`. The status is printed but never asserted, and nothing confirms that the not-found body was served. account/page.tsx calls notFound() for a classic viewer, which streams HTTP 200 with the not-found metadata and robots noindex (S6-PLAN A2/A3). A broken /account would pass this line.
fix: Assert res.status() === 200 and a positive not-found marker, such as the 'noindex, nofollow' robots meta or the not-found page's own words. Add a control in the same section: the same GET sent with the pass cookie must contain 'journey-account-hub'.

where: scripts/qa-journey-shell.mjs: §0 mintStaffPass(), and the header section's first demoSession() with a balance (live/journey-pass.mjs:62 and :88)
problem: The first compiles of the dev-test routes go through shared helpers that use Playwright's default 30 s request timeout, on a server the usage requires to start cold.
evidence: journey-pass.mjs:62 (seed-admin) and :88 (seed-wallet) post with no timeout option, so the 30 s default applies. The draft's first dev-test request is mintStaffPass() in §0; if it times out, 0.1 FAILs and every journey section is BLOCKED. The first seed-wallet call comes in the header's 999999 state; if it times out, that state's 24 tiles (the widest figure) are lost. The draft's own requests get 240-300 s, but these two do not.
fix: Before minting, warm each dev-test route the helpers use with a request that has no side effects, for example ctx.request.get(BASE + '/api/dev-test/seed-admin', { timeout: 300_000 }) and the same for /api/dev-test/seed-wallet. A POST-only route answers 405 once it has compiled. Alternatively, give the two helper posts an explicit 240 s timeout in a separate change.

where: scripts/qa-journey-shell.mjs: §11, line 11.1
